title: Elements, Tags, and Attributes
description: Understand the syntax anatomy of HTML elements, opening vs closing tags, void elements, key-value attributes, and hierarchical DOM nesting rules.

objectives.statement: Differentiate between opening tags, closing tags, elements, and void elements with 100% accuracy.
Construct syntactically valid HTML elements with correctly formatted attribute name-value pairs.
Construct clean, validly nested hierarchical DOM element structures without overlapping boundaries.

content.title: The Building Blocks: HTML Markup
content.hook: Every button, image, paragraph, and form on the web is represented as an HTML element.
content.context: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) gives structure to raw text by wrapping content in tags. The browser reads this structured markup to construct the Document Object Model (DOM) tree in memory. Understanding the precise anatomy of tags, elements, and attributes is the first essential step in becoming a frontend engineer.
goals: Differentiate between an element, an opening tag, a closing tag, and a void element.
Construct syntactically valid HTML attributes using key-value pairs.
Nest HTML elements hierarchically without syntax errors or boundary overlaps.

content.title: Element Anatomy: Tags, Attributes, and Content
content.text:
An HTML element is the complete component representing a node in the web page. It typically consists of three parts: 1. Opening Tag — Starts the element, sets the tag name, and holds any attributes. Example:

2. Content — The text or nested child elements enclosed inside. Example: Welcome to Forge 3. Closing Tag — Denoted by a forward slash (/) before the tag name, marking the end of the element. Example:

Putting it all together:

Welcome to Forge

Attributes supply extra configuration and metadata. They are always placed in the opening tag using the format name="value". Void Elements: Certain elements like , ,
, and
cannot contain content or child nodes. In HTML5, void elements never have closing tags.

content.title: Lesson Summary & Element Anatomy Takeaways
takeaways:
Element vs Tag: A tag (

or

) defines a boundary; an element is the complete component including opening tag, attributes, inner content, and closing tag.
Attributes: Configured as name="value" pairs exclusively in opening tags to provide metadata, identifiers (id), classes (class), and resource links (href, src).
Void Elements: Elements like and cannot contain children and never have closing tags in HTML5.
Hierarchical Nesting: Child elements must open and close cleanly within parent boundaries without cross-boundary overlapping (LIFO: Last In, First Out).
